summary: Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She served as a researcher and Director of Research at CNRS and as Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.
Christmas Humphreys was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as President of the Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983.

Christof Zotter works in Indology and religious studies. Attested in 2018, he has served as a postdoctoral researcher and head of the editorial program at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and on the Documenta Nepalica Book Series editorial board.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA at the University of Vienna and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier, later joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2014.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. He served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from circa 1993 to 2013.

Christoph Emmrich is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels in 2004, held a post there in 2001, and is attested as an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto.

Christoph Harbsmeier is a scholar of Sinology and linguistics educated at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen. He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980, later holding advisory professorships in China.

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Marburg. He held posts at the University of Munich, the University of Leipzig, and the Hobogirin Institute.

Christoph Theodosius Walther was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied theology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720. He later served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was an anthropologist, Indologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Vienna under Leo Frobenius and Robert von Heine-Geldern, and at the LSE. He was a professor at Osmania University and Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London.

Christophe Jaffrelot is an Indologist who studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca. He joined Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991 and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London circa 2012.

Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who has held academic posts at KU Leuven as a Sanskrit professor (attested 2009), the Université catholique de Louvain as a professor (attested 2013), and Ghent University as an associate member (attested 2026).

Christopher Andreas Holmboe was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal Frederick University and in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at the University of Oslo.
Christopher Byrne is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University, where he studied under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he has studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at the University of New Mexico. He holds a faculty position in philosophy and religious studies at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia under the academic mentorship of David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State University and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later serving as an editor and faculty member at Indiana University Bloomington.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound from 1987 to 1995 and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, earning his PhD in 2018 under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn.
